$description: MFB Brand Tokens (W3C Design Token Community Group format). Canonical source of truth: Figma 'My First Bitcoin_Full Brand Assets' (file mFIc75UUSyftaqnNUQgjLX). This file is the code-side mirror of the Figma variables; edit it ONLY to match Figma, never the other way around.

purple-400.$description: Accent dark purple — deep contrast, footer backgrounds

purple-200.$description: Accent light purple — secondary headings, gradient endpoint

orange-400.$description: Accent dark orange — hover/active states, strong emphasis

mfb.note: Deprecated 2026-07-14: appears nowhere in the canonical Figma file.

angle-base.$description: Brand slant, as a MAGNITUDE. The parent skew is negative and the counter-skew on child content is positive: skewX(calc(-1 * var(--sg-angle-base))) on the container, skewX(var(--sg-angle-base)) on the content inside it, or the text comes out slanted. So -13deg in a stylesheet is CORRECT, and the value to be suspicious of is any magnitude that is not 13. Stated here because a reader given only "13deg" cannot tell which sign the transform wants, and that ambiguity is the one this whole token set exists to remove.

mfb.note: Stated as English prose in the brand book, not as a transform. Also at 918:4219 and 918:3789. The only machine-readable -13deg rotation in the Figma file is a MISUSE example (918:2783, 'Don't place the logo on an angle'). No machine can verify this.

angle-alt.$description: Spotlight second cut. Must differ from angle-base.

mfb.note: Not in the brand book: node 918:3637 says only 'two diagonal cuts with different angles' and names no number. The nearest drawn construction line (918:3645) measures -21.9deg. Quentin's decision 2026-08-19: keep 24deg and record it as declared rather than invent provenance. On the list of what Figma owes.

logo-icon-h.$description: Brand base unit. Height of the logo icon.

base-h-ratio.$description: Parallelogram base height as a multiple of the logo icon height.

mfb.note: Brand book: 'base height = 2x the height of the logo icon'.

aspect.$description: Default supergraphic container aspect ratio, width over height.

halftone-highlight.$description: Halftone highlight cap. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: supergraphics.css:270-274 warns these are book-specified standalone values and must NOT be 'corrected' to purple-200/purple-400. Kept out of the palette deliberately.

halftone-highlight-full.$description: Halftone highlight cap for full portraits (the subject fills the frame). Cutout portraits use halftone-highlight. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: Brand Book Halftones slide, text node 918:3737: 'Cutout portraits: Highlights #F7E6FF, Shadows #45265B. Full portraits: Highlights #EEEEEE, Shadows #45265B'. Read through the Figma MCP on 2026-10-06. The shadow is the same halftone-shadow for both. Kept out of the palette, like halftone-highlight.

halftone-shadow.$description: Halftone shadow underlay and dot grid. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: See halftone-highlight. Do not fold into the palette.

highlighter-coverage.$description: Share of the word's width the highlighter line covers, centred, so it starts a little in from the first letter (10%) and stops short of the last (90%).

mfb.note: Brand Book Highlighter slide: 'Apply it to only one word per heading, covering up to 80% of the word length. Do not alter its appearance.' Measured on the same slide (Highlighter slide 918:2874, lines 918:2883 (on purple-300), 918:2887 (on orange-300), 918:2893 (on grey), 918:2898 (on white)): 79.8%, 82.5% and 82.7% of the ink width, 77.0% to 81.1% of the advance width, starting 8.1% to 9.4% in from the left ink edge. Brand in Use (918:3514, 918:4458) departs from this (70% to 88%); the slide is treated as normative.

highlighter-aspect.$description: Highlighter line length over its thickness (bounding height). The Brand Book draws the thickness in proportion to the line's length, not to the font size: at 80% coverage the line is about 3% of the word's width thick.

mfb.note: Measured from the vector geometry through the Figma MCP (read only). 26.6 on 918:2883 and 918:2898 (Education, the same geometry), 26.2 on 918:2887 (convince), 27.7 on 918:2893 (Unconference); 28.1 to 29.3 in Brand in Use. A fixed em thickness would read too thin under long words (Unconference is 0.187em).

highlighter-offset.$description: Distance of the highlighter line's centre below the text baseline. The line straddles the baseline and sits mostly below it, behind the glyphs.

mfb.note: Measured from node geometry with IBM Plex Sans metrics (baseline 0.875em below the line top at 100% line height), checked against the renders within 0.015em. Centre 0.034em, 0.029em and 0.020em below the baseline on 918:2883, 918:2887 and 918:2893; 0.020em to 0.047em across all 12 instances in the Brand Book (median 0.032em).

highlighter-shape.$description: Outline of the highlighter line in its bounding box, as a CSS clip-path: a filled quad that tapers from 6/7 of the box height at the start to 4/7 at the end, rises slightly to the right and has slant-cut ends.

mfb.note: All 12 highlighters in the Brand Book are one vector ('Vector 384') copied and scaled, drawn beneath the text in layer order. Corners taken from the SVG paths of 918:2883, 918:2887, 918:2893, 918:2898, 918:3518, 918:3574, 918:4475, 918:4501 and 918:4509. Variants: 918:3537 and 918:3559 put the top-left x at 0.71%; 918:4463 has y fractions 0.20 and 0.53.

$verification: Colour and the two IBM Plex Sans families are checked weekly against Figma page 262:2 by verify-brand-tokens.mjs, which counts rendered solid fills. That is the ONLY machine-checkable provenance in this file. Every token now carries $extensions.mfb.sourceKind: rendered-fill (checkable), prose (stated in the brand book as English, a human transcribed it, unverifiable by machine), declared (exists only downstream; this is the list of what Figma owes), measured (read off the brand book's vector geometry by a person, with the node ids in the note; no machine re-checks it), or unverified (provenance never established). Geometry added 2026-08-19: it had never been in the pipeline, which is why five different slant angles reached production.
